decisions.text: type bar: parts compared precisely: a regular bar chart, the only one whose parts share a baseline (G1.35)
values on both sides of zero: room at both ends
nominal categories sorted by value, descending
last: Net income (catch-all, missing, total, then values not known)
every name fits under its bar, neighbours at least 10 pt apart (wrapped: Product sales, Consulting income, Admin expenses, Cost of goods, Net income): vertical bars
5 values against 6 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: $3.7 million, $3.6 million, −$0.6 million, −$2.2 million, $4.5 million (G6.16, G7.4)
wrapped onto two lines: Product sales, Consulting income, Admin expenses, Cost of goods, Net income
every label just outside its bar's end: neither the text grey nor white reads on the bar's colour at 4.5 : 1 (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “income”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude
